Viewing the targets

Before shooting, the targets are shown: this is the presentation. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ it happens on each stand. In Compak® Sporting by squad, where a squad of at most six shooters moves along the stations, it happens only once a day, for the first squad. In line it works differently (see below). The presentation lets you read each target: its line, speed and distance, and what the clay does in the air.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

On each stand, the first shooter of the squad sees all the trajectories, standing ready on the stand.

Compak® Sporting

By squad: only once a day, in the morning, for the day's first squad. The shooter on station 1 calls singles A to F. In line: see below.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

You may ask the referee to show a target again: at most two more times for each target on the stand's menu.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 16 · Presentation of targets

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Doubles on report (the second target leaves when you fire at the first) are not shown. You have already seen their targets, though: a double only uses targets thrown as singles from the same stand. The first shooter of each squad is shown the simultaneous doubles (both targets leave together) and rafale doubles (two targets from the same trap, one after the other). On request they are shown again, at most twice.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 16 · Which doubles are shown

Compak® Sporting

By squad, the singles are followed by the simultaneous doubles of stations 1 to 5. After that you will hear 'start' or 'competition' from the referee, and the scored shooting begins.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 17 · Squad: showing the targets

Compak® Sporting

Compak® Sporting can also be shot in line: shooters step onto station 1 one by one and move along the line to station 5. Before the start, the first shooter may ask to see singles A to F; with simultaneous doubles, the doubles of each station are shown too. While the line fills up, each new shooter on station 1 first sees the opening target of their double. As the line empties, the referee does the same at the later stations. Details: Chapter 17 · In line with doubles on report, Chapter 17 · In line with simultaneous doubles, Chapter 17 · Closing the line.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 17 · In line with doubles on report

Safety: In both disciplines, guns stay open and unloaded during the presentation and any interruption. Close yours only when the referee allows it.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Firing, or mock shooting (mounting and swinging the gun along the target's line without a shot), while the targets are shown is forbidden. It is penalised like a gun-position offence: a warning first, then a red card.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 16 · Presentation of targets

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

If a trap breaks down or shooting stops for more than 10 minutes, the stand's targets are shown again.

Compak® Sporting

After a break of more than 10 minutes, the referee shows the six singles once more.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Nobody may practise on the competition layouts.

Compak® Sporting

You may practise on the competition trajectories, but not with the competition menus. The trajectory setting tables (ready-made menus that say which traps are shot from each station) must be different for practice. At continental and world championships, the official practice starts on the Saturday before the event.

Tip: Use the presentation to plan each target. Note where you will first see it clearly, the pick-up point, and where you will break it, the break point. Many coaches suggest also choosing the order for a simultaneous double while you watch.

How to read a target from the presentation: How to read a target.

Key points

  • Sporting™: on each stand, the first shooter of the squad sees all the trajectories, standing ready.
  • Sporting™: on request, up to two repeats for each target of the menu.
  • Sporting™: doubles on report are not presented; the first shooter of each squad sees the simultaneous and rafale doubles.
  • Compak® Sporting by squad: the targets are presented once a day, in the morning, for the first squad only. After a break of more than 10 minutes, the referee presents the six singles once more. In line has its own order.
  • Guns stay open during the presentation; in Sporting™, firing or mock shooting at that time is penalised.

Did you know?

In Sporting™ the menu in front of each stand lists the traps in shooting order and marks special targets, such as a battue or a rabbit.

Stand Talk

  • Shooter Show me the targets, please.

    Meaning: Shooter to referee: start the presentation.

  • Shooter Again, please, B only.

    Meaning: Request to repeat one target of the menu.

  • Referee Guns open during the show.

    Meaning: Referee: open and unload until the referee allows closing.

  • Coach Watch where it turns.

    Meaning: Coach in training: notice the point where the clay changes direction or shape.

  • Referee Start! / Competition!

    Meaning: Referee: the presentation is over and scored shooting begins.

For the interpreter
  • In training, viewing is the coach's favourite moment: 'watch where it turns'. In competition the presentation is part of the event, so the coaching ban applies: stay quiet unless the referee or the shooter needs a translation of procedure.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. In Sporting™, which doubles are NOT shown at the presentation?

    1. Simultaneous
    2. Rafale
    3. On report
    4. None of them
    Answer

    On report

    In Sporting™ doubles on report are not presented; simultaneous and rafale doubles are. A double only uses targets already thrown as singles on that stand.

    Chapter 16 · Which doubles are shown

  2. In Compak® Sporting by squad, how often are the targets presented?

    1. Before each squad, on each station
    2. Once a day, for the first squad
    3. Only when a shooter asks for it
    Answer

    Once a day, for the first squad

    There is one presentation a day, in the morning, for the first squad; after a break of more than 10 minutes the referee presents the six singles once more.

    Chapter 17 · Squad: showing the targets

  3. In Sporting™, during the presentation a shooter closes the gun and swings along a target's line. What applies?

    1. Forbidden: a warning, then a red card
    2. Allowed: viewing is free practice
    3. The target is shown again
    4. Only the coach gets a warning
    Answer

    Forbidden: a warning, then a red card

    Guns stay open during the presentation, and firing or mock shooting is penalised like a gun-position offence.

    Chapter 16 · Presentation of targets
